newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Kidnappers free Dutch couple in Costa Rica.
newsitem.headline: Kidnappers free Dutch couple in Costa Rica.

text.p: A Dutch couple kidnapped last month in northern Costa Rica were freed on Tuesday after payment of a ransom, police said.

The couple, named by police as Hurte Sierd Zylstra and his wife Jetsi Hendrika Coers, were freed safe and sound shortly before 6 p.m. local time (midnight GMT), Manuel Alvarado, director of Costa Rica's Judicial Investigation Organisation, told reporters.
"They are being taken to a doctor to be examined and then will give a statement to judicial authorities," Alvarado said.
Alvarado said a ransom in dollars had been paid for the release of the two Dutch citizens, both aged 50, but declined to say how much it was.
Unconfirmed news reports in Costa Rica say the kidnappers, who called themselves the "Maria Felix Commando", had asked for $600,000.

Alvarado said police exchanged fire with the kidnappers after the ransom was paid, at a location near Costa Rica's northern border with Nicaragua, but that the kidnappers fled into dense jungle and got away.
A big police operation was under way to try and catch them and the government had also asked for the help of Nicaraguan authorities, he added.
Costa Rica says the kidnappers were former Nicaraguan guerrillas who have turned to common crime.
The couple were kidnapped on the night of August 24-25 at a teak plantation they managed near the village of Aguas Zarcas de San Carlos, near the Nicaraguan border.

A Swiss tour guide and a German tourist, both women, were kidnapped in the same area earlier this year. The leader of that gang, who released their captives after almost 80 days, is under arrest in San Jose.
